I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor.

When Hannah asked me to give this speech, she said, “Just be yourself.” Then she added, “But remember, my grandparents will be there.” So this is the family edition of our friendship.

There are so many things I love about Hannah. She’s funny, thoughtful, and the person you want beside you when life gets complicated. She’s also the person who says, “Let’s get one dessert and share it,” which is the only time her judgment has ever concerned me.

One of my favorite memories with Hannah is from a moving day that went spectacularly badly. There were boxes everywhere, we couldn’t find the screws for the furniture, and I was beginning to wonder whether living out of suitcases was a perfectly reasonable long-term plan.

Hannah ordered pizza, cleared a little space on the floor, and sat down beside me. Before long, we were laughing and eating dinner off a cardboard box labeled “IMPORTANT.”

Which, apparently, contained three candles and a swimming costume.

I remember that afternoon because she made an overwhelming day feel manageable. Hannah has done that for me more times than I can count. She shows up, she listens, and somehow, even in the middle of a mess, she finds something worth laughing about.

Then Andrew came along.

When Hannah first started talking about him, she tried to sound casual. Unfortunately, it’s difficult to sound casual when you’ve mentioned someone seven times in a conversation about buying groceries.

And once I got to know Andrew, I understood.

Andrew, you pay attention to Hannah. You listen to her stories, you appreciate her humor, and you’re wonderfully willing to join in when we find something funny that probably stopped being funny ten minutes earlier.

I’ve loved getting to see your friendship grow alongside your love. You enjoy being together in a way that makes everyone around you feel comfortable, too. Watching you today, exchanging those looks and making each other smile, has been a joy.

Hannah, being your best friend has given me some of the happiest memories of my life. I’m so grateful for all the ordinary afternoons, long conversations, and ridiculous adventures we’ve shared. Standing beside you today is something I’ll treasure.

Andrew, I’m very glad you’re in her life—and in ours. I look forward to many more dinners together. We can probably find a proper table for the next one.

Please raise your glasses.

To Hannah and Andrew: may you keep finding reasons to laugh together, may you take good care of each other, and may you always order enough dessert for two.

To the newlyweds!"}
